catalog_quote: The accent presents no difficulties, since it rests almost invariably on the first syllable, if a word consists of two, three or more syllables. [p. 4] Verba commencing with the syllable com, ca, ce, as com areshe, odabeuhe, cenauhe, are accented on the second syllable. Exceptions to these two rules will be found accented in the vocabulary. [p. 5, scanned de-garbled]

tone_statements.quote: Tal es el caso del tono: en el análisis fonológico que se presenta en las notas se identifican dos tonos, uno ascendente y otro descendente, aunque de rendimiento funcional muy restringido, característica que, según en los estudios posteriores -como el realizado por esta investigadora en la década del ochenta-, ya no fue posible identificar.
tone_statements.translation: Such is the case of tone: the phonological analysis presented in the [field] notes identifies two tones, one rising and one falling, though of very restricted functional load, a feature which, according to later studies - such as the one carried out by this researcher [Fernández Garay] in the 1980s - could no longer be identified.

tone_statements.citation: Viegas Barros, J. Pedro (2015). Proto-Chon: fonología, morfología y léxico. Buenos Aires: Universidad de Buenos Aires. xix+607 pp.
tone_statements.quote: Según Suárez (1970, 1973), el tehuelche tiene dos tonos (tono a nivel y tono descendente), que tendrían un bajo nivel de rendimiento funcional. Los únicos pares mínimos ofrecidos afectan a vocales largas: ... já: `el mío’ jà: `yo’ / má: `el tuyo’ mà: `tú’ / tá: `el suyo’ tà: `él, ella’ ... Es decir, no todas las sílabas tehuelche tendrían tono contrastivo. Fernández Garay, en cambio, no encuentra oposición de tonos en tehuelche: esta autora no registra los pares mínimos establecidos por Suárez.
tone_statements.translation: According to Suárez (1970, 1973), Tehuelche has two tones (level tone and falling tone), which would have a low functional load. The only minimal pairs offered involve long vowels: ... já: 'mine' jà: 'I' / má: 'yours' mà: 'you' / tá: 'his/hers' tà: 'he, she' ... That is, not all Tehuelche syllables would have contrastive tone. Fernández Garay, by contrast, finds no tonal opposition in Tehuelche: she does not record the minimal pairs established by Suárez.
tone_statements.locator: Cap. IV, 5.2.2 'El tono en tehuelche' with Cuadro 4.40 (contents: p. 155)
tone_statements.summary: Reports Suárez's two tones (level vs falling; low functional load; only accented syllables bear tone; roots classed by tone+stress) against Fernández Garay, who found pitch non-distinctive, conditioned by glottals; author blames semi-speaker attrition and compares 164 tone-marked cognate syllables.

sources.note: Tonogenesis paper: Proto-Chon high vs low tone (*é *á *ó / *è *à *ò) from close vs open vowels; Tehuelche forms cited (āxe, tēP, Pōjo), its own system not stated here. Same author's ch. 10 (pp. 115, 117-118) states it: two tones, level and falling (per Suárez), on a morpheme's first syllable.

tone.quote: El propósito del presente trabajo es proponer una hipótesis para explicar el origen del tono en la lengua ancestral del taxón lingüístico chon de la Patagonia y Tierra del Fuego. ... Hasta donde se conoce, el günün a yajüch no tenía tonos a nivel fonológico. El proto-chon, en cambio, habría poseído dos tonos fonológicos, uno alto y otro bajo (Viegas Barros, 2022) ... las cuatro lenguas chon: teushen y aonekko ’a’ien (conocida tradicionalmente como tehuelche) en la Patagonia continental, selk’nam (también llamada ona) y haush (o manekenkn) en la Isla Grande de Tierra del Fuego
tone.translation: The aim of this paper is to propose a hypothesis to explain the origin of tone in the ancestral language of the Chon linguistic taxon of Patagonia and Tierra del Fuego. ... As far as is known, Günün a yajüch had no tones at the phonological level. Proto-Chon, by contrast, would have had two phonological tones, one high and one low (Viegas Barros 2022) ... the four Chon languages: Teushen and Aonekko ’a’ien (traditionally known as Tehuelche) in continental Patagonia, Selk’nam (also called Ona) and Haush (or Manekenkn) on Isla Grande, Tierra del Fuego
